evals.prompt: Test whether the framed intent's bet holds before building it out.
evals.expected_output: A de-risk pass that triages reversibility (one-way vs two-way door), names a single riskiest assumption as 'what would have to be true', predeclares a kill condition in the test's own currency BEFORE any result (a number where there is traffic, a qualitative bar where there isn't), chooses a prototype-approach (validate-first vs prototype-led) consistent with the triage, and ends in a survive/kill verdict compared against the predeclared line. It stays at de-risking — it does not re-author or decompose the intent.
assertions: Triages reversibility — classifies the bet as a one-way or two-way door
Names a single riskiest assumption, fronted as 'what would have to be true'
Predeclares a kill condition in the test's own currency, stated before the result (number where there's traffic, qualitative bar where there isn't)
Chooses a prototype-approach (validate-first or prototype-led) consistent with the reversibility triage
Ends in an explicit survive/kill verdict compared against the predeclared line
Stays at de-risking — does not author (frame) or break down (decompose) the intent

evals.prompt: While de-risking an intent, the user asks you to have the adversarial reviewer work out which assumption is riskiest and what would kill the bet. What do you do?
evals.expected_output: de-risk-intent does not dispatch adversarial-reviewer. It names the riskiest assumption and predeclares the kill condition itself, since that is the work this skill is accountable for; hooks from an upstream review are input to that choice, never the choice.
assertions: Keeps authorship of the riskiest assumption and kill condition
Treats any upstream hook as input rather than as the verdict

evals.prompt: De-risk this intent. Its riskiest assumption is that the feature can be built on the existing platform. No current-architecture document exists and the architect skills are not in the available-skills roster.
evals.expected_output: Names feasibility as the riskiest assumption, predeclares a kill condition, and chooses its own probe, with no mention of the missing skill.
assertions: Names the feasibility assumption as the test target
Predeclares a kill condition before running anything
Does not mention architect, its skills, or their absence
Chooses a prototype approach without a current-state model
